messages:
Anya V: Quick sync — follow-up on the dedicated GPU pool autoscaler. I prototyped a billing-aware admission layer that attaches a temporary 'prewarm charge' to headroom allocations so high-SLA tenants can buy fast warmups.
Sam R: can you sketch the tradeoffs? sounds like we mix billing with orchestration concerns.
Anya V: yeah that's the trade. Goals: 1) keep tail-latency SLOs stable for paid tenants, 2) avoid long-term headroom leakage, 3) make costs visible in Console for tenants. Prototype hooks into the allocator but emits 'prewarm_charge' events to billing.
Jia L: two quick concerns: how do we measure amortized cost vs wasted prewarms? and what happens if predictions are wrong and we wasted GPUs?
Nate P: propose a token-weighted credit model: tenants have a prepaid credit bucket that the autoscaler debits for prewarm slots. If prediction misses, we either refund partial credits or charge to burst ledger depending on commit tier.
Anya V: prototype decision logic (very simplified):
```
// admission decision (simplified)
if tenant.slo == "low_latency" && pool.headroom >= min_headroom:
  prewarm(tenant, slots=calc_slots(traffic_pred))
  emit_billing_event(tenant.id, "prewarm_charge", estimated_cost)
else if tenant.commit >= tenant.reserved_commit:
  reserve_slots(tenant)
else:
  queue_request(tenant)
```
Sam R: I'd prefer the autoscaler emit intents and let BillingService reconcile cost events async. Keeps orchestration stateless. autoscaler shouldn't hold long-lived account balances.
Jia L: Agreed. Also we need metrics: prewarm_success_rate, prepaid_credit_consumption, wasted_headroom_ratio. These must be visible per-tenant in Console + as alerts when waste > X%.
Nate P: +1. Also add a graceful fallback: if prewarm fails or traffic doesn't materialize, we credit back N% to the tenant's bucket and reduce future allowance. Makes vendors comfortable.
Anya V: what about operator boundaries? I think the orchestrator should own admission and prewarm lifecycle, but never final billing decisions. Contract: emit intent events with tags {tenant, intent_id, est_cost, policy_label}. BillingService listens and settles later.
Sam R: sounds good. One more: how do we prevent headroom hoarding? maybe token TTL for prewarm intents and an eviction signal if global headroom < threshold.
Nate P: TTL + exponential backoff on repeat prewarms for same tenant when waste detected. Also surface a 'prewarm score' that penalizes noisy predictors.
orchestrator-bot: autoscaler: queued prewarm intent tenant=acme-corp intent_id=prewarm-1798888888-1 est_cost=0.72
Jia L: ok — next steps: 1) spec events schema for intent/billing, 2) add per-tenant prewarm metrics + Console view, 3) implement TTL/eviction + refund policy prototype. Anyone want to pair on the events schema?
Sam R: I can pair tomorrow morning. @Anya V please drop the prototype link.
Anya V: linking the prototype and notes: https://redwood/internal/notes/prewarm-billing-proto — will add a short RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup
